_comment: THE PERMITTED LIST (st_dd0e19d8 AC15). Every entry here is a DELIBERATE WEAKENING
of the publication gate. Read it that way.
An entry says: this exact TERM, in this exact FILE, from this exact CLASS, is not a
leak — and here is why. Scoped per term AND file AND class, never a bare term: a
bare-term suppression is the failure mode that let one dead rule silently hide 184
later real findings in the study this design is built on.
DECAY. Every publication run removes entries that no longer match anything, scoped to
the paths that run actually scanned — so an entry covering a file the run did not look
at is neither matched nor removed. The list cannot fill up with dead rules.
WHAT MAY LIVE IN THIS FILE. This file is TRACKED and it ships in the published
repository, so an entry publishes both its term and the statement that the term is a
member of an owner-corpus class. Entries for the owner-identifying classes (terms,
private_terms, domains, entity_ids, paths) are therefore REFUSED here and belong in
the gitignored config/publication-permitted.user.json. And every term named here must
already appear, in cleartext, in the tracked file the entry names — a permitted entry
may only excuse an exposure the tree already has, never create one.
Both rules are enforced: node scripts/check-publication-permitted.js --schema
Five of the entries below sit in files the pre-commit hook regenerates and stages
DURING the commit (public-truth, llms-full, the FAQ bundle and context). Without them,
promoting the address class to blocking at commit time would fail every commit the
owner makes, because the hook itself puts the address back.

permitted.reason: the product's public support address, printed on the public licensing page. It is in the owner corpus only because it is also his own mailbox; it is published on purpose.
public support address in the published privacy policy — the contact a reader is meant to use.

public support address inside the generated public-truth corpus. Regenerated and staged by the pre-commit hook, so it returns on every commit.

public support address in the generated FAQ context. Regenerated and staged by the pre-commit hook, so it returns on every commit.

public support address in the generated FAQ bundle. Regenerated and staged by the pre-commit hook, so it returns on every commit.
